title: Disseminated Tuberculosis With Ocular Involvement After 12 Years of Anti-TNF- α Therapy.
abstract: Background Ocular tuberculosis (TB) is an uncommon yet potentially vision-threatening manifestation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis , particularly difficult to diagnose in immunocompromised individuals. The increasing use of anti-tumor necrosis factor- α (anti-TNF- α ) agents has markedly heightened the risk of TB reactivation, often with disseminated or extrapulmonary involvement despite negative baseline screening. Case presentation We describe a 52-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis receiving long-term adalimumab and methotrexate who developed disseminated TB with pulmonary, splenic, and ocular involvement after 12 years of anti-TNF- α therapy. Baseline screening had shown a negative tuberculin skin test and an indeterminate interferon- γ release assay. She presented with constitutional and respiratory symptoms, whereas chest computed tomography demonstrated diffuse micronodular infiltrates consistent with miliary TB. Microbiological confirmation was obtained via bronchoalveolar lavage. Ophthalmologic evaluation revealed bilateral choroidal granulomas with subretinal edema, leading to a diagnosis of ocular TB. Standard antitubercular therapy (ATT) was initiated but required modification due to drug-induced liver injury. Adjunctive systemic corticosteroids were introduced after antimicrobial therapy and gradually tapered. The patient achieved progressive clinical, radiological, and ophthalmologic improvement, with gradual regression of choroidal lesions. Discussion This case underscores the persistent long-term risk of TB reactivation during prolonged anti-TNF- α therapy and highlights the limitations of current screening strategies in immunosuppressed patients. Ocular TB requires integration of systemic, clinical, and imaging findings; in this patient, microbiologically confirmed disseminated TB together with characteristic bilateral choroidal granulomas supported a definitive diagnosis. Management relies on prompt ATT, discontinuation of immunosuppression, and judicious use of adjunctive corticosteroids. Long-term follow-up is essential given the risk of persistent lesions and late recurrence. Reintroduction of biologic therapy may be feasible in selected cases but requires careful risk stratification. Conclusion TB should remain a diagnostic consideration in patients receiving biologic therapy who develop compatible systemic or ocular manifestations, even after long-term treatment and negative baseline screening. Close multidisciplinary collaboration is essential for the diagnosis and management of ocular TB in this population.

Ocular tuberculosis (TB) is an uncommon yet potentially vision-threatening manifestation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, particularly difficult to diagnose in immunocompromised individuals. The increasing use of anti-tumor necrosis factor-α (anti-TNF-α) agents has markedly heightened the risk of TB reactivation, often with disseminated or extrapulmonary involvement despite negative baseline screening.

We describe a 52-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis receiving long-term adalimumab and methotrexate who developed disseminated TB with pulmonary, splenic, and ocular involvement after 12 years of anti-TNF-α therapy. She presented with constitutional and respiratory symptoms, whereas chest computed tomography demonstrated diffuse micronodular infiltrates consistent with miliary TB. Microbiological confirmation was obtained via bronchoalveolar lavage. Ophthalmologic evaluation revealed bilateral choroidal granulomas with subretinal edema, leading to a diagnosis of ocular TB. Standard antitubercular therapy (ATT) was initiated but required modification due to drug-induced liver injury. Adjunctive systemic corticosteroids were introduced after antimicrobial therapy and gradually tapered. The patient achieved progressive clinical, radiological, and ophthalmologic improvement, with gradual regression of choroidal lesions.

This case underscores the persistent long-term risk of TB reactivation during prolonged anti-TNF-α therapy and highlights the limitations of current screening strategies in immunosuppressed patients. Management relies on prompt ATT, discontinuation of immunosuppression, and judicious use of adjunctive corticosteroids. Long-term follow-up is essential given the risk of persistent lesions and late recurrence. Reintroduction of biologic therapy may be feasible in selected cases but requires careful risk stratification.

TB should remain a diagnostic consideration in patients receiving biologic therapy who develop compatible systemic or ocular manifestations, even after long-term treatment and negative baseline screening. Close multidisciplinary collaboration is essential for the diagnosis and management of ocular TB in this population.

title: Pediatric Dilated Cardiomyopathy With Suspected Hereditary Protein C/S and Antithrombin III Deficiency Presenting as Ischemic Stroke-A Rare Case Report.
abstract: Objective To report a rare case of pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with suspected hereditary protein C, protein S, and antithrombin III deficiency presenting as ischemic stroke. Background Children with DCM are at increased risk of thromboembolism. Inherited thrombophilias are an uncommon but important cause of pediatric stroke and may coexist with cardiac disease. Case presentation An 8-year-old female presented with heart failure and was diagnosed with severe DCM (LVEF ∼24%). Despite medical therapy and antiplatelet prophylaxis, she developed acute right-sided hemiparesis. MRI confirmed a left hemispheric ischemic stroke. Thrombophilia workup revealed reduced protein C (41.5%), protein S (50.7%), and antithrombin III (65.1%) levels, suggestive of a suspected inherited thrombophilic disorder, while PT/aPTT/INR remained normal. She was managed conservatively with antiplatelets and rehabilitation, showing partial neurological recovery. Follow-up demonstrated improved cardiac function (LVEF ∼50%). Conclusion The coexistence of DCM and suspected inherited thrombophilia can predispose to ischemic stroke in children. Normal routine coagulation tests do not exclude thrombophilia; targeted screening should be considered in high-risk cases.

title: A Case of Misdiagnosed Pediatric Congenital Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus due to AQP2 Variants.
abstract: Background Congenital nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (CNDI) is a rare disorder of renal water handling, often presenting in early infancy with severe polyuria and hypernatremia. Differentiating CNDI from central diabetes insipidus (CDI) remains challenging, and delayed identification may result in inappropriate therapy, leading to adverse growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes. Case presentation We present the case of an 8-month-old male infant with a history of suspected CDI since birth. He was treated with desmopressin (dDAVP) without clinical benefit. The absence of the posterior pituitary bright spot at magnetic resonance imaging supported the CDI diagnosis. Considering persistent polyuria with recurrent episodes of hypernatremia and low urine osmolality, a diagnosis of CNDI was proposed, and plasma copeptin (CP) levels were determined. Measurement of CP showed markedly increased concentrations, suggesting renal tubular resistance to vasopressin. dDAVP therapy was discontinued and patient's management was adjusted to include hydrochlorothiazide therapy and a high-calorie diet restricted in sodium and protein. The patient showed progressive clinical improvement with reduction of polyuria and stabilization of serum sodium levels, although linear growth delay persisted. A final diagnosis of CNDI was confirmed by molecular analysis that identified rare compound heterozygous variants in the AQP2 gene, c.85G > A variant (maternal) and c.553C > G (paternal). Conclusions This case highlights the diagnostic pitfalls of CNDI in infancy and underscores the pivotal role of early CP assessment and molecular genetic testing in distinguishing CNDI from CDI. Prompt recognition of CNDI is essential to avoid ineffective dDAVP therapy and to initiate a targeted multidisciplinary approach. Rare AQP2 mutations further expand the genotypic spectrum of CNDI and emphasize the need for heightened clinical awareness and early referral to specialized centers.

title: Hyperactive Delirium Temporally Associated With Hydroxyzine in a Child With Succinic Semialdehyde Dehydrogenase Deficiency Presenting With Psychotic Symptoms: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) metabolism caused by biallelic variants in ALDH5A1. The phenotype includes developmental delay, intellectual disability, seizures, sleep disturbance, anxiety, and other neurobehavioral symptoms. Psychotic symptoms are increasingly recognized in SSADHD but remain uncommon and incompletely characterized in children. In medically and neurodevelopmentally vulnerable patients, acute psychiatric decompensation may also be complicated by delirium, especially when severe sleep-wake disruption, poor intake, constipation, metabolic stress, and potentially deliriogenic medications are present. Case presentation We describe a 12-year-old girl with intellectual disability, global developmental delay, abnormal prior neuroimaging, abnormal EEG findings, progressive weight loss, reduced oral intake, insomnia, and new-onset auditory and visual hallucinations. During hospitalization, she developed a fluctuating neurobehavioral syndrome marked by impaired attention, severe sleep-wake disruption, increased startle response, inconsolability, agitation, perceptual disturbances, and waxing and waning behavioral organization. These findings supported hyperactive delirium superimposed on psychotic symptoms rather than isolated psychosis. Hydroxyzine was ordered as 25 mg by mouth every 6 h as needed and was administered six times from hospital day 5 through early hospital day 7. The medication provided mixed short-term anxiolytic and sedating benefits but did not meaningfully reduce hallucinations or restore normal sleep. After hydroxyzine exposure, impaired attention, profound sleep-wake dysregulation, inconsolability, increased startle response, fluctuating agitation, and behavioral disorganization remained prominent, raising concern that hydroxyzine may have contributed to persistence or worsening of the acute confusional state in the setting of severe sleep deprivation, poor oral intake, constipation, neurologic vulnerability, and underlying SSADHD. Hydroxyzine was discontinued, and low-dose quetiapine was initiated together with environmental sleep-wake and reorientation interventions. Sleep, appetite, oral intake, and behavioral regulation subsequently improved. Diagnostic evaluation supported SSADHD, including elevated urinary 4-hydroxybutyric acid, characteristic MRI abnormalities of the globi pallidi and dentate nuclei, and a homozygous ALDH5A1 missense variant, NM_001080.3:c.434A >G (p.Glu145Gly), formally classified as a variant of uncertain significance but considered clinically concordant with the diagnosis. Conclusion This case highlights SSADHD as an important consideration in children presenting with acute psychotic symptoms and altered mental status. It also underscores the importance of distinguishing psychotic symptoms from superimposed delirium in developmentally vulnerable patients. Because hallucinations, insomnia, poor intake, and behavioral dysregulation preceded hydroxyzine exposure and several competing contributors were present, hydroxyzine should be framed as a possible exacerbating or prolonging factor rather than the definitive sole cause of delirium. The case is therefore best described as hyperactive delirium temporally associated with, and possibly exacerbated by, hydroxyzine exposure.

title: Rapunzel Syndrome as a Complication of Childhood-Onset Trichotillomania.
abstract: Introduction Rapunzel syndrome is a rare and potentially life-threatening complication of trichotillomania with trichophagia, characterized by the extension of a gastric trichobezoar into the small intestine. Diagnosis is frequently delayed due to nonspecific presenting symptoms, and management requires both surgical intervention and psychiatric treatment to prevent recurrence. Patient case We report the case of a 22-year-old woman with childhood-onset trichotillomania and trichophagia who presented with nonspecific abdominal complaints. Imaging revealed a large intragastric mass, and endoscopy confirmed a dense trichobezoar extending through the pylorus into the duodenum, consistent with Rapunzel syndrome. Endoscopic removal was unsuccessful, and the patient underwent open gastrotomy with intact removal of the mass without complication. Psychiatric evaluation revealed a long history of hairpulling and ingestion behaviors beginning in early childhood, with limited prior psychiatric treatment. Discussion This case illustrates the cumulative medical risk of untreated chronic, childhood-onset trichotillomania with trichophagia, particularly when hair-ingestion behaviors persist without sustained trichotillomania-specific behavioral treatment. Its contribution to the literature lies in the detailed longitudinal psychiatric characterization of symptom progression and the consideration of comorbid attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), which may be relevant to the hairpulling and ingestion behaviors themselves through attentional dysregulation, impulsivity, impaired inhibitory control, and automaticity. Conclusion Rapunzel syndrome represents a severe consequence of chronic hairpulling and ingestion behaviors. Early identification of trichophagia, psychiatric referral, and sustained behavioral treatment are essential to prevent progression to life-threatening complications and to reduce recurrence following surgical intervention.

title: Atraumatic Spontaneous Splenic Rupture Complicating Decompensated Chronic Liver Disease With Portal Hypertension: A Case Report.
abstract: Atraumatic spontaneous splenic rupture (ASR) is a rare, potentially fatal condition accounting for fewer than 0.5% of all splenic ruptures, with reported mortality of up to 20% when diagnosis is delayed. We report a 63-year-old male with decompensated chronic liver disease and portal hypertension who presented with acute epigastric pain, progressive abdominal distension, and absolute constipation without antecedent trauma. Abdominal ultrasonography identified splenomegaly with a 5 × 6 cm anechoic intraparenchymal collection with subcapsular and perisplenic extension and moderate hemoperitoneum. Noncontrast computed tomography confirmed parenchymal laceration classified as AAST Grade III/WSES Class II. Contrast-enhanced CT was deferred because of concurrent renal impairment. The patient remained hemodynamically stable and was successfully managed with conservative nonoperative management. This case highlights the importance of suspecting ASR in patients with hepatic disease and congestive splenomegaly without trauma, the utility of prognostic scoring in guiding management, and the role of contrast-enhanced ultrasound as a nephroprotective imaging alternative when iodinated contrast is contraindicated.

title: A Rare Autoimmune Triad: Coexistence of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Sjögren's Syndrome, and Ankylosing Spondylitis: A Case Report.
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), Sjögren's syndrome (SS), and ankylosing spondylitis (AS) are distinct immune-mediated diseases with different classification frameworks and usual treatment approaches. Coexistence of all three disorders in a single patient is rare and creates diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report a 40-year-old woman with longstanding SLE, SS associated with SLE, and subsequently recognized axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA)/AS. The patient fulfilled the 2019 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for SLE (total score ≥ 10), the 2016 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for primary SS (total score ≥ 4), and the 2009 ASAS classification criteria for axSpA through both the imaging and clinical arms. Conventional treatment options were limited by prior gastrointestinal bleeding with NSAIDs and concern for drug-induced lupus-like syndromes with TNF inhibitors. The patient remained stable on hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily and was enrolled in a Phase 2 SLE clinical trial evaluating a JAK inhibitor. Treatment assignment was unknown during the blinded period; during the unblinded continuation phase, she was confirmed to be receiving upadacitinib 15 mg daily. Over a 6-month duration of confirmed upadacitinib exposure, clinical improvement in lupus- and sicca-related symptoms were observed, and follow-up MRI showed resolution of previously documented sacroiliitis. Although causality cannot be established from a single uncontrolled observation, the clinical and imaging improvement during confirmed upadacitinib exposure is hypothesis-generating and suggests that shared inflammatory pathways may warrant further investigation in selected overlap cases.

Treatment assignment was unknown during the blinded period; during the unblinded continuation phase, she was confirmed to be receiving upadacitinib 15 mg daily. Over a 6-month duration of confirmed upadacitinib exposure, clinical improvement in lupus- and sicca-related symptoms were observed, and follow-up MRI showed resolution of previously documented sacroiliitis. Although causality cannot be established from a single uncontrolled observation, the clinical and imaging improvement during confirmed upadacitinib exposure is hypothesis-generating and suggests that shared inflammatory pathways may warrant further investigation in selected overlap cases.

title: Hepatic B-Cell Lymphoma in a Common Mynah ( Acridotheres tristis ): A Case Report.
abstract: Background Hepatic lymphoma is rarely characterized in mynah birds, and severe hepatomegaly in this group is often interpreted in relation to iron storage disease or other metabolic hepatopathies. Case description This report describes hepatic B-cell lymphoma in a 14-year-old common mynah ( Acridotheres tristis ) presented with lethargy, altered vocalization, poor body condition, ascites, dyspnea, chronic ataxia, and left-leg lameness. Radiography revealed a large soft-tissue opacity in the middle coelomic cavity, with caudodorsal displacement of the intestinal loops and compression of the thoracoabdominal air sacs. Ultrasonography identified a very large hepatic mass with granular and mixed echogenicity occupying most of the coelomic cavity. The bird was euthanized at the owner's request because of the severity of the lesion and poor clinical condition. At necropsy, the liver was markedly enlarged, dark red to reddish-brown, mottled and occupied most of the coelomic cavity. Histologically, the hepatic parenchyma was extensively replaced by densely packed mononuclear neoplastic cells, with effacement of hepatic cords and hepatocellular necrosis. No neoplastic infiltration was identified in the examined tissues, including spleen, kidney, intestine, lung, and heart; therefore, the liver was the only confirmed site of lymphoma among the examined tissues in this case. An immunohistochemical and histochemical panel including CD3, CD79 α /MB-1, CD20, lysozyme, CD68, alpha-1-antitrypsin, toluidine blue, and Giemsa staining was applied to characterize the tumor lineage and exclude other round-cell neoplasms. Neoplastic cells showed diffuse cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for CD79 α /MB-1 and lacked evidence of T-cell, monocyte/macrophage, or mast cell differentiation, supporting a diagnosis of hepatic B-cell lymphoma. Conclusion This case highlights the need for tissue-based diagnosis in mynah birds with marked hepatomegaly and demonstrates the value of integrating diagnostic imaging, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing in avian hepatic round-cell tumors.

title: Generalized Megaesophagus Concurrent With Toxocariasis in a Cat.
abstract: Feline megaesophagus is a rare disorder characterized by esophageal hypomotility and dilation, resulting in regurgitation, weight loss, and occasionally death. This report describes the clinical and paraclinical findings of generalized megaesophagus with a possible contribution of toxocariasis in a kitten. A 2-month-old female cat was referred with chief complaints of lethargy, hyporexia, dyspnea, and vomiting/regurgitation. Physical examination of the kitten revealed bradycardia, bradypnea, hypothermia, dehydration, and lung crackles. The most notable laboratory results were leukopenia with severe toxic changes in neutrophils. Radiographic findings were compatible with the diagnosis of generalized megaesophagus. Despite supportive measures, the kitten died the next day. Necropsy revealed diffuse esophageal dilation and Toxocara spp. roundworms in the stomach and duodenum. Histopathology showed an ascarid larva in the esophagus, necrosis and metaplasia in the pylorus, and absence of villi and Brunner's glands in the duodenum. Based on the morphological identification of the adult gastrointestinal nematodes, the final diagnosis was generalized megaesophagus of unspecified classification concurrent with toxocariasis. However, the exact cause of death could not be established. Although respiratory abnormalities raised suspicion of a pulmonary complication, pneumonia was not confirmed. We hypothesized that toxocariasis may have contributed to esophageal dysfunction in this kitten through potential mechanisms such as vomiting, gastrointestinal obstruction, or neurological involvement; however, these mechanisms could not be directly demonstrated. Therefore, parasitic diseases, including toxocariasis, may be considered among potential differential diagnoses or contributing conditions in young cats presenting with megaesophagus, particularly when concurrent gastrointestinal parasitism or related complications are identified. Further studies are required to clarify the possible relationship between toxocariasis and esophageal dysfunction.

title: Coil Embolization and Open Splenectomy for a Massive Splenic Vein Aneurysm: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Splenic vein aneurysms (SVAs) are a rare vascular anomaly of the portal system that are often asymptomatic and found incidentally on imaging. Intervention is reserved for aneurysms that are enlarging, thrombosed, symptomatic, or ruptured to avoid catastrophic complications. This can range from endovascular to open, complex procedures. Here, we present the case of a massive, symptomatic, partially thrombosed SVA that required a hybrid approach involving both minimally invasive and open surgery. Case presentation A 56-year-old woman presented to the emergency department for an infected right foot wound and was admitted for intravenous antibiotics and surgical debridement. While hospitalized, she had a worsening transaminitis with associated abdominal pain, prompting investigation with a computed tomography (CT) scan, which identified a massively dilated, partially thrombosed SVA measuring 18 cm. Given the enormous size of the aneurysm and substantial risk of impending rupture, urgent surgical intervention was planned. Preoperative coil embolization of the splenic artery was performed first to reduce the arterial inflow to the SVA and to minimize the risk of intraoperative hemorrhage during open resection. Three days after embolization, the patient underwent open splenectomy with aneurysmectomy for definitive management. The patient's postoperative course was complicated by a bleeding gastric ulcer that was successfully cauterized, and she was discharged home on postoperative Day 10 after receiving the recommended postsplenectomy vaccines. Conclusion No standard treatment algorithm exists for SVAs, as management is individualized, and treatment evidence is limited to case reports and series. This patient had one of the largest SVAs ever recorded, and management was based on the acuity of symptoms, size, and rupture risk of the aneurysm sac. This case also demonstrated the success of a novel management approach to massive SVAs, using preoperative embolization of the splenic artery followed by open resection without portal reconstruction.

title: Next-Generation Sequencing to Identify Genetic Causes of Chinese Patients Affected With Non-retinal Developmental Eye Disorders.
abstract: To investigate the genetic causes of non-retinal developmental eye disorders in 14 Chinese different families, we subjected participants to a specific hereditary eye disease enrichment panel (HEDEP) or whole exome sequencing. We further validated disease-causing variants and performed co-segregation analyses on the available family members by Sanger sequencing. We classified sequence changes according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association for Molecular Pathology variant interpretation guidelines. Fourteen probands with diverse clinical diagnoses were analyzed, including microphthalmia (with or without microcornea and congenital cataract or congenital corneal opacification (CCO), four cases), anterior segment dysgenesis (ASD, six cases)-including Peter's anomaly (PA, one case), PA and microphthalmia (one case), iridocoloboma or aniridia (with microcornea and/or congenital cataract, two cases), and primary congenital glaucoma (PCG, two cases)-congenital cataract (with CCO or microcornea, three cases), and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RSTS, one case). Initial inheritance patterns for 1, 5, and 8 cases were autosomal recessive, autosomal dominant, and sporadic, respectively. We identified 17 (likely) pathogenic variants and one variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in 16 genes, including BMP4 , BCOR , PITX3 , and PAX6 . Among them, eight were novel variants, and two were de novo . We confirmed the pathogenicity of PAX6 intronic mutation using in vitro splice assays and redefined the pathogenicity of the variants of uncertain significance as likely pathogenic. Patients with developmental eye diseases typically have complex ocular and systemic phenotypes, possibly leading to significant visual impairment and high blindness rates. Identifying the genetic causes facilitates early diagnosis and effective treatment and rehabilitation strategies, thereby providing valuable insights for genetic and clinical counseling of these patients.

title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlations and Their Implications for Personalized Genetic Counseling in 103 Patients With PRRT2 Mutations.
abstract: Objective PRRT2 mutations are associated with a wide spectrum of paroxysmal neurologic disorders. In this study, we analyze clinical and genetic data from a large pediatric cohort to define genotype-phenotype correlations and to provide a basis for individualized genetic counseling. Methods This retrospective study included 103 children with PRRT2 mutations treated at the Children's Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing Medical University from August 2018 to August 2023. Detailed clinical data and genetic results were collected and systematically analyzed. Results Among the 103 children, self-limited familial infantile epilepsy (SeLFIE) was the most common phenotype. A total of 26 different PRRT2 mutations were identified, 93.2% of which were predicted loss-of-function (LOF) mutations. These mutations were highly enriched in the N-terminal cytoplasmic region of the protein, particularly in the proline-rich domain. Predicted LOF mutations accounted for nearly all cases of SeLFIE and infantile convulsions with paroxysmal choreoathetosis. Clinical features, including age of onset, rates of abnormal EEG and brain MRI findings, and treatment response, showed a gradient across the three phenotypic groups, with the most pronounced abnormalities in SeLFIE and the mildest in paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia. Additionally, 12 novel variants were identified. Conclusion This study confirms that PRRT2 -associated disorders are primarily driven by predicted LOF mutations and, using a large cohort, establishes a genotype-phenotype-treatment response continuum model based on residual PRRT2 protein activity. This model provides a critical framework for prognosis assessment and personalized genetic counseling.

title: The Prevalence of Histologically Confirmed Endometriosis in Salpingectomy Specimens for Hydrosalpinx and Subsequent Reproductive Outcomes.
abstract: Background Hydrosalpinx, a fluid-filled blocked fallopian tube, is a major cause of infertility and is mainly linked to pelvic inflammatory disease. However, its connection to endometriosis, especially hidden tubal endometriosis without visible signs, is not well studied. This research aimed to find the prevalence of confirmed endometriosis in salpingectomy samples removed due to hydrosalpinx and to evaluate the subsequent reproductive outcomes. Methods A cross-sectional study involved 70 infertile women undergoing laparoscopic salpingectomy at a specialized center. We gathered demographic, surgical, and pathological information from medical records. The main outcome was the occurrence of endometriosis based on histopathology. The secondary outcome was the rate of clinical pregnancies (either spontaneous or through ART) after salpingectomy. We used SPSS v23.0 for statistical analysis, considering p < 0.05 as significant. Results The average age of participants was 37.38 ± 6.13 years. Clear histological evidence of endometriosis was found in 14.3% (10/70) of samples. Notably, 8% (4/50) of patients without a history of endometriosis had hidden tubal disease. The visual detection of endometriosis during laparoscopy was marginally significantly associated with a positive pathology (37.5% vs. 7.4%, p = 0.050). After salpingectomy, the total clinical pregnancy rate was 25.5% (12/47). However, none of the patients (0%) with a diagnosis of tubal endometriosis achieved pregnancy, while those with other pathologies had a 30% success rate. Conclusion Examining salpingectomy samples is essential for detecting endometriosis. Women with histologically confirmed tubal endometriosis may represent a subgroup with potentially poorer reproductive outcomes. However, this observation is exploratory and requires validation in larger studies with adequate adjustment for age, ovarian reserve, and ART-related factors.

title: Using FIT Thresholds for Priority Triage and Risk Stratification in Resource-Constrained Systems.
abstract: In many colorectal cancer screening settings, a key issue is no longer whether fecal immunochemical testing (FIT) should guide access to colonoscopy, but how FIT results can be used more effectively to manage limited colonoscopy resources. The article by Wu and colleagues provides important data showing the predictive potential of using quantitative FIT (qFIT) values for subsequent risk of colorectal cancer in a hospital-based screening setting. Although colonoscopy is the gold standard for screening, it is costly, invasive, and becoming increasingly constrained by aging populations, expanded screening eligibility, and an increasing number of postpolypectomy surveillance colonoscopies. Unlike binary positive or negative results, qFIT can provide a more refined measure of fecal hemoglobin and underlying colorectal cancer risk. Higher qFIT values are associated with advanced neoplasia and colorectal cancer, which can allow screening programs to prioritize those at greatest short-term risk for faster follow-up procedures. Evidence suggests that FIT positivity thresholds can be tuned to optimize colonoscopy resources and screening goals. In settings where there is a growing burden of postpolypectomy surveillance colonoscopy, FIT-based triage provides a low-cost strategy to improve efficiency, reduce wait times, and maximize the yield of endoscopy resources. Moving beyond binary FIT toward quantitative or risk-based screening follow-up pathways has the potential to optimize colonoscopy allocation and improve overall screening system performance. See related article by Wu et al., p. 733 .

title: Individual and Occupational Factors Associated with Receipt of Guideline-Concordant Cancer Screening in California Firefighters.
abstract: Background Firefighters face elevated cancer risk due to occupational exposures, yet cancer screening adherence and associated factors remain poorly characterized. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of survey data from 3,076 active-duty career firefighters in California without a prior cancer diagnosis. Screening adherence was evaluated against U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) and National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) guidelines for colorectal (CRC), breast, cervical, prostate, skin, and lung cancer. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the associations between screening receipt and demographic, occupational, behavioral, clinical, and health belief factors. Results Overall, screen-eligible participants were racially/ethnically diverse (25% Hispanic; 37% non-White), had a mean age of 41 years, and a mean tenure in the fire service of 17 years. Receipt of guideline-concordant screening varied by cancer type and guideline: CRC (54% NFPA, 68% USPSTF), breast (76%), cervical (75%), prostate (59% NFPA, 78% USPSTF), skin (29%), and lung (ever low-dose computed tomography, 10%). Older age (odds ratio [OR]=1.19-2.65 per 5 years), 1+ years since a routine doctor's visit (OR=0.36-0.58), and family history of cancer (OR=1.33-1.77) were consistently associated with receipt of cancer screening. Conclusions Firefighters who were younger (yet within eligibility age range), had not recently engaged in routine healthcare, and did not have a family history of cancer were less likely to be screened. Impact This is the first broad characterization of cancer screening among career firefighters, identifying potentially actionable targets for interventions to close screening gaps in this high-risk population.

title: Longitudinal liquid biopsy and matched radiomic analysis indicated resistance mechanisms of patients with biliary tract cancer undergoing systemic treatment.
abstract: Background and aims Data on the evolution of molecular alterations during first-line systemic anti-cancer treatment (SACT) are lacking for biliary tract cancers. Liquid biopsy and radiomics are non-invasive tools that could provide insights. Methods Plasma samples collected at baseline (N=39) and progressive disease (PD, N=30) were subjected to NGS panel covering SNV and CNV [Avenio ctDNA-Expanded-kit]. CT scans were reviewed for total tumor burden (TTB) analysis and for an exploratory radiomic analysis. Results cfDNA concentration correlated with TTB (p=0.0003). Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas (iCCA) had larger TTB (p=0.034) and higher number of alterations (p=0.02). cfDNA concentration or median dominant VAF did not correlate with outcomes. Baseline MET SNVs (p=0.07) and ERBB2 CNVs (p=0.03) were associated with shorter time to progression (TTP). iCCA frequently displayed a heterogeneous molecular response to SACT. Patients with increasing CNV score for EGFR [TTP: 4.1 vs 9.5 months, p=0.003; overall survival (OS): 10.1 vs 21.6 months, p=0.02] and MET [TTP: 4.2 vs 10.1 months, p=0.01; OS: 9.5 vs 20.2 months, p=0.06] had worse outcomes than those with decreasing score during SACT. Cases with PD driven by EGFR and MET were associated with selected baseline radiomic features: NGTDM Coarseness (p=0.041), GLSZM Zone Size Entropy (p=0.028) for EGFR; GLRLM Short Run Emphasis (p=0.034), GLRLM Run Length Variance (p=0.017), GLRLM Run Entropy (p=0.028), GLSZM Large Zone Emphasis (p=0.019) for MET. Conclusion Liquid biopsy identified potential primary (MET SNVs/ERBB2 CNVs) and secondary (EGFR/MET CNVs) resistance mechanisms to platinum-based SACT. Radiomics provided an early correlation with molecular evolution.

title: [18F]RCCB6 PET/CT in Diagnosing Clear-Cell Renal Cell Carcinomas: A Prospective Comparison Study with [18F]FDG PET/CT and Conventional Imaging.
abstract: This single-center prospective phase II trial evaluated [18F]RCCB6 (renal cell carcinoma B6) positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT), a cluster of differentiation 70 (CD70)-targeting radiotracer, for detecting metastases in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). After screening 291 patients, 150 patients with histologically confirmed ccRCC or suspected kidney cancer underwent imaging. Among 1,221 assessable extrarenal lesions, [18F]RCCB6 PET/CT achieved 94.2% sensitivity, 80% specificity, 93.1% accuracy, and 98.3% positive predictive value. In a head-to-head comparison of 99 patients with 683 lesions, [18F]RCCB6 significantly outperformed 2-deoxy-2-[fluorine-18]fluoro-D-glucose ([18F]FDG) PET/CT, with higher diagnostic sensitivity (90.5% vs. 41.1%) and specificity (81.4% vs. 24.3%; both P < 0.001). Compared with conventional imaging across 748 lesions, [18F]RCCB6 PET/CT also demonstrated superior sensitivity (90.8% vs. 75.1%) and specificity (81.6% vs. 56.6%). [18F]RCCB6 uptake (maximum standardized uptake value) strongly correlated with CD70 expression (r = 0.843; P < 0.001). Moreover, the imaging findings changed clinical management in 58.7% of patients. [18F]RCCB6 PET/CT is a highly sensitive imaging modality for diagnosing ccRCC metastases and informing clinical decision-making. Significance This phase II trial demonstrates that [18F]RCCB6 PET/CT significantly outperforms conventional imaging and [18F]FDG PET/CT in detecting metastatic ccRCC, with 94.2% sensitivity and strong correlation with CD70 expression, altering clinical management in 58.7% of patients.

title: Prevalence and Diagnostic Performance of the BRAF V600E Mutation in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma: A Cross-Sectional Study in Uruguay.
abstract: Thyroid cancer is the most common endocrine malignancy, and the detection of thyroid nodules has increased with the widespread use of ultrasound. In this context, the BRAF V600E mutation has emerged as an important molecular marker in papillary thyroid carcinoma; however, its prevalence varies geographically and local data remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of the BRAF V600E mutation in a Uruguayan population and to evaluate its potential role as a complementary diagnostic tool. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted including 155 patients who underwent fine-needle aspiration (FNA) for thyroid nodules at Maciel Hospital between October 2020 and September 2022). Archived formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor samples were also analyzed to increase the number of histologically confirmed cases. Detection of the BRAF V600E mutation was performed using allele-specific PCR. Clinical, ultrasonographic, cytological (Bethesda classification), and histopathological data were collected from medical records. The prevalence of the BRAF V600E mutation was 75.9% among 29 papillary thyroid carcinomas and only 4/151 benign lesions (2.6%). The assay showed a sensitivity of 73.3% (CI 55.6% - 85.8) and a specificity of 95.4% (IC 90.7% - 97.7%), with a positive predictive value of 75.9% (CI 57.9% - 87.8%) and a negative predictive value of 94.7 (CI 90.0% - 97.3%) Significant associations were observed between the mutation and Bethesda categories V-VI (p < 0.001), hypoechogenicity (p = 0.01) and malignant histopathology (p < 0.001). These findings support the use of BRAF mutation testing may serve as a complementary tool in the diagnostic assessment of thyroid nodules.

title: The Solitary Functioning Kidney: From Pathophysiology to Long-Term Management.
abstract: Solitary functioning kidney (SFK) is a clinical condition characterized by the presence of a single functioning kidney, arising from either congenital anomalies or acquired causes. It is recognized as an important risk factor for chronic kidney disease (CKD) and, in some patients, for progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). Congenital solitary functioning kidney is commonly associated with renal hypoplasia or dysplasia, genetic abnormalities, and congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract, whereas acquired solitary functioning kidney is often secondary to unilateral nephrectomy for renal tumors, trauma, tuberculosis, severe infection, or living kidney donation. The principal pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the progression from SFK to CKD are compensatory renal hypertrophy and glomerular hyperfiltration in the remnant kidney. Although these adaptive responses may initially maintain renal function, sustained compensation can lead to glomerular injury, proteinuria, tubulointerstitial damage, and renal fibrosis. Early diagnosis relies primarily on imaging modalities, such as ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging, together with assessment of renal function and emerging biomarkers, including neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and cystatin C. Prognostic evaluation of patients with SFK should comprehensively consider etiology, age, compensatory renal growth, associated urinary tract anomalies, comorbidities, and markers of kidney injury. Effective long-term management is essential to prevent or delay progression to CKD and ESKD, with particular emphasis on individualized follow-up, lifestyle modification, blood pressure control, reduction of proteinuria, and avoidance of additional nephrotoxic insults. Previous publications have often addressed pediatric congenital solitary functioning kidney (CSFK), living kidney donors, and disease-related nephrectomy cohorts separately, limiting the translation of heterogeneous evidence into a common clinical approach. This review integrates congenital and acquired SFK across the life course, distinguishes shared markers of established kidney injury from etiology-specific determinants of renal reserve, and proposes an evidence-informed framework for dynamic risk stratification and risk-adapted follow-up and management. This framework is conceptual and requires prospective validation.

title: Kidney Volumetry for Predicting Long-Term Outcome in Acute Kidney Injury: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Introduction Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is effective for severe acute kidney injury (AKI); however, predicting successful CRRT discontinuation and long-term outcomes remains challenging. Although urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) levels and kidney volume measured by computed tomography (CT) have been associated with renal prognosis, it remains unclear whether their combination improves predictive accuracy. This study evaluated whether combining urinary NGAL levels with kidney volume measured by CT improves prediction accuracy. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, urinary NGAL levels and height-adjusted total kidney volume (HtTKV) were assessed for their ability to predict successful CRRT discontinuation and major adverse kidney events at 90 days (MAKE90). Results Among the 74 patients included, CRRT discontinuation was successful in 55 (74.3%), and MAKE90 occurred in 31 (41.9%). Urinary NGAL (area under the curve [AUC], 0.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.76-0.95) was a significant predictor of CRRT discontinuation, whereas HtTKV was not. For long-term outcomes, urinary NGAL (AUC, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.61-0.85]) and HtTKV (AUC, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.54-0.80]) were significantly associated with MAKE90. Adding HtTKV to urinary NGAL significantly improved the prediction of MAKE90, as demonstrated by reclassification analyses (net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement). Conclusions Adding HtTKV significantly improved the prediction of long-term MAKE90 based on NGAL levels, but not that of short-term CRRT discontinuation. These findings in this proof-of-concept study suggest that structural kidney assessment by CT volumetry may complement urinary NGAL for long-term risk stratification in patients with severe AKI requiring CRRT.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery from the Left Coronary Sinus.
abstract: Introduction Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery (AAORCA) is a rare congenital anomaly that may be associated with adverse cardiac events, including sudden cardiac death. Surgical correction is commonly recommended in patients with AAORCA. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a prevalent diagnostic modality, which increases AAORCA detection. However, the clinical significance of incidentally detected AAORCA remains unclear. Methods This non-randomized retrospective analysis included 10,134 patients who underwent CCTA between January 2014 and December 2022, either for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) or a medical check-up. Three groups were created: patients with normal coronary anatomy (normal), with AAORCA (anomaly), and CAD without AAORCA (CAD). CAD was defined as a percentage diameter stenosis of ≥50% in one or more segments. Cardiac mortality was this study's primary endpoint. Results Normal, anomaly, and CAD group comprised 7592 (74.9%), 66 (0.7%), and 2476 (24.4%) patients, respectively. During a median follow-up of 33.7 months (IQR: 13.2-53.4), Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed no significant difference in the cardiac death occurrence between the normal (15 events, 0.2%) and anomaly groups (0 events, 0%) (log-rank p=0.685). Cox proportional hazards model revealed no difference in mortality in the anomaly group compared with normal group. Conclusions In our cohort, incidentally detected AAORCA in adults did not demonstrate a clearly elevated cardiac death risk relative to CAD during mid-term follow-up. However, given the small number of events, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive rather than confirmatory evidence of a benign natural course, particularly in populations at higher risk of exertional sudden cardiac death.

title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems for Secondary Caries Detection and Staging on Bitewings: A Multi-Algorithm Comparison.
abstract: Introduction Radiographic detection of caries lesions adjacent to restorations is challenging because of the limitations of two-dimensional imaging and difficulties distinguishing true lesions from restorative or anatomical radiolucencies. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based clinical decision support systems (CDSSs) have been introduced to assist radiographic interpretation; however, different AI tools may yield variable diagnostic outputs, and their comparative performance remains unclear. Objective To compare the diagnostic performance of commercial and experimental AI algorithms for detecting and staging secondary caries lesions on bitewings. Methods This cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study included 200 anonymized bitewings comprising 885 restored tooth surfaces. A consensus-based reference standard classified each restored surface as non-carious, secondary caries, or indeterminate. Secondary caries lesions were further staged as enamel-stage or dentin-stage. Five commercial AI systems (Second Opinion®, CranioCatch, Diagnocat, DIO Inteligência, and Align™ X-ray Insights) and three experimental systems based on Mask R-CNN and Mask DINO architectures were tested. Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value (95% confidence intervals). Comparisons were performed using generalized estimating equations adjusted for clustered data. Results Specificity was high across all systems (0.957-0.986), whereas sensitivity was moderate (0.327-0.487), reflecting missed detections of secondary caries lesions, particularly dentin-stage lesions. Accuracy ranged from 0.882 to 0.917, with no significant differences among the evaluated systems (p ≥ 0.05). Similar patterns were observed in the additional analysis restricted to dentin-stage lesions. Misclassifications between non-carious and secondary caries surfaces were frequently associated with radiographic overlap, restoration-related radiolucencies, and cervical artifacts. Conclusions AI algorithms, regardless of architecture or commercial status, showed similar diagnostic capabilities and a conservative diagnostic profile, favoring specificity over sensitivity. Improvements in dataset diversity, reference-standard quality, and model explainability may further enhance the reliability of AI-assisted secondary caries detection.

title: Diagnostic performance of ICDAS for root caries: comparison with histological reference standards.
abstract: Introduction Evidence regarding the performance of visual test for root caries severity assessment is still limited. This in vitro diagnostic performance study evaluated visual test with ICDAS (International Caries Detection and Assessment System) root criteria against three histological reference standards -stereomicroscopy (SM), polarised-light microscopy (PLM), and micro-computed tomography (micro-CT). Methods A total of 125 extracted permanent teeth were classified with the visual test using ICDAS root criteria. Histological evaluation was performed using SM and PLM. In addition, in a subsample of 22 teeth was assessed further using micro-CT. Discriminative power, global and categorised performance (confidence interval with a 95% confidence level) and agreement (Cohen's Kappa and percentage), and indicators of validity and diagnostic utility (sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values - PPV and NPV, likelihood ratios - LR+ and LR-) were stablished. Results Compared with histological reference standards, the visual-tactile test showed moderate to high diagnostic performance for root caries for sensitivity (≥ 0.73), specificity (≥ 0.90), and predictive values (PPV ≥ 0.71, NPV ≥ 0.91). Overall likelihood ratios supported moderate confirmatory value (LR+ = 7.43-9.39) and rule-out ability (LR- = 0.26-0.30) after visual-tactile classification. Agreement between the visual test and the histological references was substantial (weighted kappa ≥ 0.88), with moderate discriminative power (0.63-0.68). Complete observed agreement was found for the sound category. Performance was high for initial caries (≥90% for sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values; LR+ ≥10; discriminative power ≥0.82), whereas extensive lesions showed good rule-out ability but lower confirmatory value. Conclusion The visual-tactile test showed substantial agreement against histological reference standards, moderate to high diagnostic performance, and moderate discriminative power. The test showed complete observed agreement for sound surfaces and high performance for identifying initial caries, whereas extensive lesions showed good rule-out ability but lower confirmatory value. These findings support the visual-tactile ICDAS root caries criteria as useful for the detection and assessment of root caries lesions.

title: Guidelines for Colonic Diverticular Disease-2026, Second Edition: Management of Diverticular Bleeding and Acute Diverticulitis.
abstract: Colonic diverticular disease is becoming increasingly common in Japan, paralleling population aging and changes in lifestyle and medication use. The predominance of right-sided diverticulosis in Asian populations, in contrast to the left-sided predominance in Western populations, influences clinical presentation and management. In Japan, diverticulitis has become a clinically important problem, and diverticular bleeding is currently the most frequent cause of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB). The Japanese Gastroenterological Association updated its clinical guidelines for diverticular bleeding and diverticulitis in 2026. Key domains including epidemiology, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, and priority clinical and future research questions were addressed. Evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach, and recommendations were formulated via a modified Delphi process with external review. These guidelines aim to provide Japanese and Asian evidence-based consensus that complements Western guidelines. Recommendations for acute LGIB and diverticular bleeding are as follows: risk stratification with the Shock Index and Oakland and NOBLADS scores guides triage; pre-colonoscopy contrast-enhanced computed tomography is the widely used diagnostic modality; routine colonoscopy within 24 h is not suggested for all patients; endoscopic band ligation or direct clipping is suggested post-detection of stigmata of recent hemorrhage; and early oral refeeding is suggested. Recommendations for diverticulitis are as follows: post-resolution colonoscopy is suggested to exclude colorectal cancer; outpatient treatment and withholding of antibiotics are suggested in selected uncomplicated cases; and primary anastomosis may be favored over Hartmann's procedure in selected complicated cases.

title: Endoscopic Treatment for Pancreatobiliary Diseases in Patients with Surgically Altered Anatomy: A Perspective from Double-Balloon Endoscopy.
abstract: Background The number of patients with surgically altered anatomy (SAA) is increasing worldwide. In these patients, pancreatobiliary disease is difficult to treat, because a conventional duodenoscope cannot reach the papilla or the bilioenteric anastomosis through the long reconstructed limb. For many years the main treatment options were reoperation or percutaneous drainage, both of which are invasive. Summary Double-balloon endoscopy (DBE), first reported in 2001, made it possible to insert the endoscope stably through the long limb and to reach the target perorally. The short-type DBE, and later a newly designed short-type DBE, then made therapeutic ERCP practical, because standard ERCP devices could be used. In a Japanese multicenter prospective study of 311 patients with SAA, the target site was reached in 97.7% (304/311) and the overall procedural success rate of 92.3% (287/311). Among the 283 patients requiring treatment, therapeutic success was achieved in 97.9% (277/283). Adverse events occurred in 10.6% (33/311), and 32 of the 33 events were managed conservatively. In this review we describe how DBE-assisted ERCP (DBE-ERCP) developed, summarize the current evidence, and discuss how it should be positioned relative to single-balloon endoscopy (SBE), interventional endoscopic ultrasound (EUS), and percutaneous drainage. Key messages DBE-ERCP and interventional EUS should be regarded as complementary approaches. DBE-ERCP is an important first-line option for many benign biliary disorders in non-Roux-en-Y gastric bypass SAA, particularly when preservation of the native papilla or surgical anastomosis and repeated intervention are important. Alternative approaches should be considered early in selected settings, including interventional EUS after failed balloon-endoscopy access or in malignant biliary obstruction, and EDGE or laparoscopy-assisted ERCP in Roux-en-Y gastric bypass anatomy when appropriate expertise is available. Treatment should be individualized according to the reconstruction anatomy, disease target, need for repeat intervention, and local expertise.

title: Endoscopic treatment strategies for gastric foveolar-type adenoma with a raspberry-like appearance.
abstract: Background/objectives Endoscopic treatment strategies for gastric foveolar-type adenoma with a raspberry-like appearance (GFA-R) have not yet been established. We aimed to clarify the efficacy and safety of endoscopic procedures for GFA-R. Methods We extracted GFA-Rs, which were pathologically diagnosed in accordance with WHO classification, at our hospital from January 2009 to December 2023 by endoscopy and retrospectively analyzed their clinicopathological features and endoscopic outcomes. Results Eighty-eight GFA-Rs were collected from 74 patients. The mean size of GFA-Rs was 4.2 mm (range, 1-10 mm). All lesions demonstrated intramucosal neoplasms without lymphovascular invasion. Endoscopic procedures included only biopsy (n=6), cold forceps polypectomy (CFP; n=42, as outpatient 38/42), cold snare polypectomy (CSP; n=4), endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR; n=36, as inpatient 36/36). The overall en bloc resection rate was 93.9 % (77/82), with rates of 92.9 % (39/42) for CFP, 75.0 % (3/4) for CSP, and 97.2 % (35/36) for EMR, respectively. Lesions smaller than 5 mm were more often treated with CFP while lesions larger than 5 mm were more often treated with EMR. No complications, such as post-operative bleeding or delayed perforation, occurred regardless of the endoscopic procedure. The mean follow-up period was 28.7 months (range, 2-165 months). No local recurrences occurred at 1 year (9-18 months) after an endoscopic procedure for 62 lesions, 2 years (19-30 months) for 40 lesions, and 3 years (31-42 months) for 24 lesions. Conclusions These results suggest that endoscopic procedures for GFA-R are effective and safe regardless of the procedure used. Moreover, outpatient CFP may be a simple, useful, and cost-effective endoscopic procedure for GFA-R smaller than 5 mm.

title: Surface-extraction MRI of the fetal brain: an improved approach for diagnosing anomalies associated with antenatal absence of the septum pellucidum.
abstract: Introduction Prenatal imaging is crucial for evaluating neurological development in cases of absence of septum pellucidum (ASP), which may be associated with a spectrum of cortical, cerebellar and ocular anomalies and variable neurodevelopmental outcomes. Recent advances in fetal MRI techniques have improved the detection and characterization of subtle brain abnormalities. Case report A pregnant patient was referred to our tertiary centre for targeted neurosonography at 28weeks of gestation, confirming ASP initially considered isolated. Fetal MRI at 33 weeks suspected associated cortical malformations, with unilateral peri-sylvian polymicrogyria and closed lip schizencephaly, but it partially limited by motion artefacts. Subsequent super‑resolution reconstruction (SRR) and cortical surface extraction confirmed the presence of polymicrogyria associated with schizencephaly. Post-MRI neurosonography also confirmed unilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria and schizencephaly. Following multidisciplinary discussion parents opted for termination of pregnancy. Post‑mortem neuropathological examination confirmed the imaging findings, demonstrating polymicrogyria associated with schizencephaly in the right perisylvian region. Conclusion This case highlights the possible added diagnostic value of advanced fetal MRI post‑processing, which enabled precise characterization of cortical abnormalities not confidently identified on conventional imaging. The strong correlation with neuropathological findings supports the potential role of surface‑based analysis in improving diagnostic accuracy and prenatal counselling in cases of ASP.

title: The fetal Ear-Eye and Ear-Rotation angle: A pilot study on novel 3D ultrasound measure-ments for prenatal diagnosis of low-set ears.
abstract: Introduction Low-set ears are frequently associated with chromosomal aberrations, congenital malformations, and genetic syndromes. While typically described postnatally, prenatal diagnosis usually relies on subjective expert pattern recognition. We introduce a standardized 3D ultra-sound measurement approach to assess fetal ear position relative to the eye and head. Methods Retrospective pilot analysis of prospectively acquired 3D head volumes (16-34 weeks; 10/2023-10/2025). The "ear-eye angle," "ear-rotation angle," and ear length were meas-ured by two blinded examiners in healthy controls and a malformation group. Results We included 102 fetuses (82 controls, 20 malformations) at a median 21 weeks' gesta-tion (16-34). The malformation group had a significantly larger median ear-eye angle than con-trols (3.29° [-2.81-7.88] vs. 1.02° [-11.04-8.75]; P<0.001) and median ear-rotation angle (17.50° [-33.75-37.20] vs. 12.10° [0.00-38.40]; P=0.029). Logistic regression showed that for every one-degree increase in the ear-eye angle, the odds of a malformation increased significant-ly (OR 1.36; 95% CI: 1.11-1.65; P = 0.002). ROC analysis revealed the ear-eye angle had supe-rior discriminative ability over the ear-rotation angle (AUC 0.76 vs. 0.66). Inter-observer agree-ment was high (ear-eye ICC=0.96; ear-rotation ICC=0.92). Conclusion Systematic evaluation of the fetal ear on routinely collected 3D volumes is feasible. Both angles were significantly larger in affected fetuses compared to healthy controls. However, due to the limited sample size and prevalence of abnormal cases, these diagnostic performance metrics should be interpreted with caution and require validation in larger cohorts.

title: Post-mortem MRI assessment of fetal corpus callosum growth patterns between 14 and 22 weeks of gestation.
abstract: Introduction The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest commissural tract in the human brain, playing a crucial role in interhemispheric communication and neurodevelopment. Although ultrasonography and MRI have been used to assess callosal morphology, most available data are from later gestational ages, with limited normative information for fetuses below 20 weeks. This study aims to fill this gap by evaluating the biometry of the corpus callosum using high-resolution post-mortem fetal brain MRI between 14 and 22 gestational weeks. Materials and methods This observational cross-sectional study analyzed post-mortem MRI scans of 77 neurotypical fetal brains aged 14-22 gestational weeks. Imaging was performed on a 3T MRI scanner using a dedicated fetal protocol. T2-weighted STIR sequences provided optimal contrast for delineating the corpus callosum. The anteroposterior (AP) length and body thickness were measured on mid-sagittal images. Data were analyzed using SPSS with descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation, linear regression, and ANOVA at a significance level of p < 0.05. Results The mean AP length of the corpus callosum was 1.78 ± 0.69 cm, and the mean body thickness was 0.171 ± 0.031 cm. AP length showed a strong positive correlation with gestational age (r = 0.952, p < 0.001), while body thickness showed a moderate correlation (r = 0.613, p < 0.001). Conclusion This study provides early normative post-mortem MRI data of corpus callosum growth between 14 and 22 weeks. The findings establish reference values that may assist in early detection of callosal dysgenesis and related neurodevelopmental abnormalities.

title: Systematic differences between ultrasound and MRI assessment of fetal ventricular width in cases of fetal mild ventriculomegaly: a cohort study.
abstract: Prenatal assessment of the lateral ventricles is essential for detecting and classifying fetal ventriculomegaly (VM). Although ultrasound (US) is the primary screening tool, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is increasingly used to complement diagnosis. However, discrepancies between US and MRI measurements, particularly in mild VM, may affect classification, counseling, and planning clinical management. The aim of the study is to compare US and MRI measurements of the fetal lateral ventricles, evaluate the agreement between both methods, with particular focus on mild ventriculomegaly, and additionally assess the feasibility of deriving conversion formulas between both modalities. Methods This cohort study included 120 fetuses examined between 2011 and 2021 at a referral center: 75 with isolated mild VM and 45 controls. All underwent a standardized US assessment and fetal MRI. Ventricular width was measured twice for each modality; mean values were used for statistical comparison. Analysis included Wilcoxon tests, Friedman tests, Bland-Altman plots, Pearson's chi-square tests, Theil-Sen regression, and linear modeling. Results MRI systematically provided greater ventricular measurements than US. In the study group, the bias was 0.71mm for coronal MRI and 0.33mm for axial MRI. Agreement between methods was limited, with measurement discrepancies observed in 34% of cases (coronal) and 33.3% (axial). Combined analysis of both groups confirmed persistent measurement discrepancies, though the overall axial MRI bias decreased to 0.15mm. Theil-Sen modelling enabled the development of conversion formulas for both measurement planes. Conclusions MRI measurements of the fetal lateral ventricles tend to be slightly higher than ultrasound measurements, particularly in the coronal plane. These systematic differences may change the VM classification and should be considered in clinical interpretation. Ultrasound demonstrated better measurement reproducibility. The obtained formulas may support improved cross-modality comparison in clinical practice.

title: Local RAGE Inhibition Attenuates Early Diabetic Retinal Pathology in Streptozotocin-Induced Rats.
abstract: Introduction Diabetic retinopathy, which occurs during extended periods of chronic hyperglycemia, is one of the main causes of vision loss. The receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE) plays a central role in inflammatory and angiogenic signaling, both of which contribute to the pathogenesis of diabetic retinopathy, but its therapeutic targeting in ocular disease has been insufficiently explored. Methods We evaluated topical RAGE229, a small-molecule RAGE inhibitor, and an intravitreally administered anti-RAGE antibody in a streptozotocin-induced diabetic rat model. At day 84, treatment effects were assessed using masked fundoscopic scoring, RT-qPCR, immunohistochemistry, and histological morphometry. Treated eyes were evaluated against both route-matched diabetic vehicle-control groups and paired contralateral vehicle-treated eyes. Results Both interventions reduced fundoscopic pathology and retinal Vegfa and Nfkb1 expression, whereas Ager showed only a non-significant downward trend. NF-κB p65 immunoreactivity was reduced by both treatments, while a significant reduction in VEGF-A immunoreactivity was detected only in the paired anti-RAGE antibody analysis. Morphometric analysis indicated attenuation of diabetes-associated retinal thinning with both interventions. Neither intervention altered systemic glycemic control. Although both interventions demonstrated similar overall anatomical protection, anti-RAGE antibody treatment showed more consistent effects across protein-level and structural endpoints. Conclusion These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence that local RAGE-targeted treatment may attenuate vascular, molecular, and structural manifestations of early experimental diabetic retinopathy without detectable changes in systemic glycemia. Further preclinical studies should evaluate ocular exposure, direct target engagement, functional visual outcomes, and reproducibility in larger cohorts.

title: Calcium Overload in Trisomy 21: An Underrecognized Cause of Persistent Hypercalcaemia - A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Calcium overload in trisomy 21 is a rare and underrecognized cause of persistent parathyroid hormone (PTH)-independent hypercalcaemia in infants and young children with Down syndrome. Characteristic features include hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, renal impairment, and failure to thrive. Delayed recognition may result in avoidable long-term complications. Case presentation A 21-month-old boy with trisomy 21 presented with a six-month history of recurrent vomiting, feeding difficulties, and failure to thrive. Bilateral nephrocalcinosis was detected incidentally on abdominal ultrasound. Laboratory evaluation revealed marked hypercalcaemia with suppressed PTH and 1,25(OH)₂D, hypercalciuria, and acute kidney injury. Extensive diagnostic work-up excluded alternative causes of PTH-independent hypercalcaemia. Nutritional assessment showed an almost exclusively milk-based diet with minimal solid food intake. Initial treatment with intravenous fluids and a single dose of pamidronate resulted in only transient improvement. Following the diagnosis of calcium overload, a calcium-restricted diet consisting of normal and low-calcium formula was introduced and adjusted according to biochemical response. Serum calcium normalized and remained stable throughout 11 months of follow-up. Growth and developmental progress improved, while nephrocalcinosis persisted and renal function partially recovered. Conclusion Calcium overload in trisomy 21 should be considered in young children with Down syndrome presenting with failure to thrive, recurrent vomiting, and nephrocalcinosis in combination with PTH-independent hypercalcemia. Early recognition and initiation of dietary calcium restriction may prevent long-term complications such as chronic kidney disease and prolonged growth impairment.

title: Development of a protocol to retrospectively identify acute traumatic brain injury using electronic medical records from an academic health system data warehouse.
abstract: Introduction As recommended in the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke TBI Classification and Nomenclature Initiative, retrospective identification of traumatic brain injury (TBI) from electronic medical record (EMR) data offers major potential for research and surveillance. Enterprise data warehouses integrating structured and unstructured EMR data could support this work, yet few studies have evaluated their use for TBI case ascertainment. This study describes a manual chart review protocol to identify acute TBI among patients receiving head CT scan from a large health system's enterprise data warehouse. Methods We identified encounters potentially related to TBI using clinical documentation files (e.g., Emergency Department Triage, History & Physical, Discharge Summary) within our institution's enterprise data warehouse. Two independent raters applied the protocol to 126 patients who presented in 2019 and underwent head computed tomography (CT). Sampling was limited to patients receiving a head CT scan to enrich the cohort with both TBI and non‑TBI cases. We developed a decision tree workflow to guide documentation of a plausible mechanism of head injury accompanied by clinical symptoms and/or clinically indicated neuroimaging. Criteria were adapted from the American Congress of Rehabilitation Medicine definition of mild TBI and modified for retrospective EMR data. Raters classified each case as (1) no evidence of acute TBI, (2) sufficient evidence of acute TBI, or (3) inconclusive evidence due to missing data or confounding conditions (e.g., syncope). Results Inter‑rater reliability demonstrated strong agreement across raters (88.1% agreement; Cohen's κ = 0.80 (95% CI: 0.71-0.89), p < 0.0001); inter-rater reliability was similar across subgroups of age (± 65 years), sex, and payor (government/non-government insurance). Among the 126 cases reviewed, there was agreement on sufficient evidence of acute TBI for 49 cases (86.0% agreement between rater 1 and 2), no evidence of acute TBI for 54 cases (96.4% agreement), and inconclusive evidence for 8 cases (61.5% agreement). Sensitivity analyses reweighting the sample to parent cohort marginal distributions produced similar results (94.2% agreement, κ = 0.74 (95% CI: 0.58-0.90). Conclusion This manual chart review protocol showed strong inter‑rater reliability for identifying acute TBI using EMR data. Future research should examine external reliability in other health systems and compare its performance with International Classification of Diseases‑based definitions and prospective diagnosis. As enterprise data warehouses become more ubiquitous, reliable case ascertainment protocols such as this could facilitate standardized, scalable retrospective identification of TBI, supporting retrospective TBI cohort studies.

title: Biomarkers and Prognostic Factors in Multiple System Atrophy: A Protocol for a Three-Year, Multicenter, Prospective, Longitudinal Cohort Study in Japan and South Korea.
abstract: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is a sporadic, adult-onset neurodegenerative disorder characterized by autonomic failure, Parkinsonism, and cerebellar ataxia. Early diagnosis remains a major unmet need because current clinical criteria often identify the disease only after considerable progression. The recently proposed Movement Disorder Society (MDS) prodromal MSA criteria provide a framework for earlier recognition; however, their specificity is limited. In particular, individuals who initially present isolated parkinsonism or cerebellar ataxia without overt autonomic dysfunction may be overlooked, although some of them eventually progress to MSA. To address this critical gap, this multinational, multicenter study aims to clarify the earliest detectable clinical and biological phases of MSA, identify predictors of disease conversion, and refine prodromal diagnostic criteria within a well-characterized East Asian cohort. This project will be conducted across multi-centers in Japan and South Korea in two phases. Phase 1 is a retrospective analysis of patients initially suspected but not diagnosed with MSA, who were later confirmed as probable or clinically established MSA, to delineate early clinical, imaging, and autonomic features. Phase 2 is a prospective longitudinal cohort enrolling patients aged 30-80 years classified as mono-system MSA (moMSA), possible prodromal MSA according to MDS criteria, or pure autonomic failure. Participants will undergo standardized clinical, neuroimaging, and biomarker assessments including serum and CSF every six months for up to 36 months to identify predictors of conversion to probable or clinically established MSA. This protocol represents the first multinational effort in East Asia to establish a longitudinal prodromal MSA cohort. By integrating clinical, neuroimaging (brain MRI), and biomarker data (α-synuclein strain and genetic analysis), the study aim to clarify the earliest detectable phase of MSA, refine prodromal diagnostic criteria, and provide a platform for future disease-modifying trials. Clinical research information service (CRIS) number: KCT0011830.

title: The prognostic impact of sarcopenia and hypoalbuminemia on overall survival in esophageal cancer: a retrospective single-center study.
abstract: : Introduction: The aim of the study was to investigate the influence of sarcopenia and hypoalbuminemia on overall survival in patients with esophageal cancer. Methods Data from 138 patients treated for esophageal cancer at the Institute of Radiation Oncology, Bulovka University Hospital, Prague, Czech Republic, between 2009 and 2018 were retrospectively analyzed. Sarcopenia was assessed using the skeletal muscle index (SMI) derived from staging CT scans at the level of the L3 vertebra. Results SMI was assessed in 129 (93.5%) patients and baseline albumin levels were available in 114 (82.6%) patients. The median overall survival was 9 months (range 1-154 months). Sarcopenia was detected in 80 patients (58.0%) and hypoalbuminemia in 38 patients (27.5%). Notably, 68.8% of sarcopenic patients had a normal or higher BMI, highlighting the limited ability of BMI alone to identify nutritionally compromised patients. Both sarcopenia and hypoalbuminemia were significantly associated with worse overall survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis (sarcopenia: p = 0.049; hypoalbuminemia: p = 0.007). On univariate Cox regression, sarcopenia showed a non-significant trend (HR 1.393, 95% CI 0.967-2.006; p = 0.075), while hypoalbuminemia was significantly associated with overall survival (HR 0.574, 95% CI 0.384-0.859; p = 0.007); neither factor retained independent prognostic significance on multivariate analysis. Conclusion Sarcopenia and hypoalbuminemia were associated with worse overall survival in our cohort of patients with esophageal cancer on univariate analysis. Given the study's limitations, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts.

title: Secondary metastasis resection after biomarker-stratified first-line treatment of metastatic colorectal carcinomaInterim analysis of the IVOPAK II study with a risk-benefit assessment of secondary metastatic resection.
abstract: Objective The IVOPAK II study (Interdisciplinary Care with Quality Control in Palliative Treatment of Colorectal Cancer) prospectively evaluated the risk (postoperative complications, mortality) and benefit (overall survival) of multimodal treatment with secondary metastasis resection for initially nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma. Patients and methods A total of 40 patients from 10 centers were enrolled. Patients with quintuple wildtype (K-RAS, N-RAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, ERBB2, MSS) received FOLFIRI plus cetuximab, while patients with RAS-mutation (K-RAS or N-RAS, MSS) received FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab. CT scans were presented at two-month intervals to the interdisciplinary tumor board at the University Hospital Erlangen to assess potentially curative secondary metastatic resection. After a median follow-up of 32 months, outcomes of the multimodally (chemotherapy treatment plus metastasis resection) and the palliatively (only chemotherapy treatment) treated patients were compared. Results The rate of secondary metastasis resection was 45% (18/40). Overall survival was significantly longer in the multimodal treatment group compared to the palliative treatment group (median 61 vs. 22 months, p=0.002), this also applied to progression-free survival (median 39 vs. 11 months, p=0.018). Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 morbidity occurred in 28% (5/18) of patients, and 90-day mortality was 6% (1/18). Univariate analyses revealed a significant improvement in overall survival among patients with ECOG performance status 0, solitary metastatic site and multimodal treatment. In multivariate analysis, the ECOG performance status proved to be an independent prognostic factor. Conclusion Following palliative biomarker-stratified first-line treatment for nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma, the multimodal approach with secondary metastatic resection demonstrated a significant survival benefit.

Objective

The IVOPAK II study (Interdisciplinary Care with Quality Control in Palliative Treatment of Colorectal Cancer) prospectively evaluated the risk (postoperative complications, mortality) and benefit (overall survival) of multimodal treatment with secondary metastasis resection for initially nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma.

Patients and methods

A total of 40 patients from 10 centers were enrolled. Patients with quintuple wildtype (K-RAS, N-RAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, ERBB2, MSS) received FOLFIRI plus cetuximab, while patients with RAS-mutation (K-RAS or N-RAS, MSS) received FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab. CT scans were presented at two-month intervals to the interdisciplinary tumor board at the University Hospital Erlangen to assess potentially curative secondary metastatic resection. After a median follow-up of 32 months, outcomes of the multimodally (chemotherapy treatment plus metastasis resection) and the palliatively (only chemotherapy treatment) treated patients were compared.

Results

The rate of secondary metastasis resection was 45% (18/40). Overall survival was significantly longer in the multimodal treatment group compared to the palliative treatment group (median 61 vs. 22 months, p=0.002), this also applied to progression-free survival (median 39 vs. 11 months, p=0.018). In multivariate analysis, the ECOG performance status proved to be an independent prognostic factor.

Conclusion

Following palliative biomarker-stratified first-line treatment for nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma, the multimodal approach with secondary metastatic resection demonstrated a significant survival benefit.
